{{nihongo|'''Matsubara Shrine'''|松原神社 (春日井市)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

It is identified with "Matsubara Tenjin" of Kasuharu District in the '{{ill|Owari Kokunai Jinmyōchō|ja|尾張国内神名帳|sv|Owari Kokunai Jinmyōchō|zh|尾張國內神名帳|qid=Q11041830}}', but another theory treats it as a {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|Q135022904|qid=Q135022904}} for "Takamu Shrine" in Kasugabe District of {{ill|Owari Province|Q514506|qid=Q514506}} in the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'.

===History===
Tradition says it was founded on {{ill|February 11 (Lunisolar)|Q839324|qid=Q839324|lt=lunar February 11}} of {{ill|Wadō (era)|Q1373026|qid=Q1373026}} 4 ({{ill|AD 711|ab|711|af|711|am|711 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|711|ar|711|ast|711|az|711|azb|۷۱۱ (میلادی)|be|711|be_x_old|711|bg|711|bn|৭১১|bpy|মারি ৭১১|br|711|bs|711.|ca|711|cdo|711 nièng|ceb|711|ckb|٧١١|crh|711|cs|711|cv|711|cy|711|da|711|de|711|el|711|eml|711|eo|711|es|711|et|711|eu|711|fa|۷۱۱ (میلادی)|fi|711|fo|711|fr|711|fy|711|ga|711|gan|711年|gd|711|gl|711|hak|711-ngièn|he|711|hi|711|hr|711.|ht|711 (almanak jilyen)|hu|711|hy|711|id|711|ilo|711|io|711|is|711|it|711|ja|711年|jv|711|ka|711|kaa|711|kk|711 жыл|ko|711년|krc|711 джыл|la|711|lb|711|lij|711|lmo|711|lt|711 m.|map_bms|711|mdf|711|mg|711|mhr|711|mk|711|mr|इ.स. ७११|mrj|711 и|ms|711|mzn|۷۱۱|nah|711|nap|711|nds|711|new|सन् ७११|nl|711|nn|711|no|711|nrm|711|nso|711|oc|711|or|୭୧୧|os|711-æм аз|pl|711|pnb|711|pt|711|qu|711|ro|711|ru|711 год|rue|711|sa|७११|sah|711|scn|711|sd|711ع|sh|711.|shn|711|si|711|simple|711|sk|711|sl|711|sq|711|sr|711|su|711|sv|711|sw|711|tg|Соли 711|th|พ.ศ. 1254|tk|711|tl|711|tly|711|tr|711|tt|711 ел|uk|711|ur|711ء|uz|711|vec|711|vi|711|war|711|wuu|711年|xmf|711|zh|711年|zh_min_nan|711 nî|zh_yue|711年|qid=Q23519}}), in the reign of {{ill|Empress Genmei|Q233224|qid=Q233224}}. Because this area was then called "Takamu," it has been thought possibly to be the "'''Takamu Shrine'''" in the Engishiki register<ref>There is still a shrine called "Takamu Shrine" in {{ill|Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Q1155291|qid=Q1155291}} of {{ill|Nagoya|Q11751|qid=Q11751}}, but it is unknown which one is the shrine listed in the Jinmyōchō.</ref>.
In the medieval period, {{ill|Inari Ōkami|Q719665|qid=Q719665|lt=Inari faith}} spread. As a result an Inari shrine was merged here as well, and it drew devotion under names such as "'''Takamu Inari Daimyōjin.'''
In {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}, this area belonged to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Inuyama Prefecture}}. In October Meiji 4 ({{ill|1871|Q7746|qid=Q7746}}), Inuyama Prefecture recognized it as the "Matsubara Shrine" in the '{{ill|Izumi Province Divine Name Register|Q11420490|qid=Q11420490|lt=Owari Kokunai Jinmyōchō}}'. Inuyama Prefecture then merged with {{ill|Nagoya Prefecture|Q11415214|qid=Q11415214}} on {{ill|November 22 (Lunisolar)|Q840493|qid=Q840493|lt=lunar November 22}} of the same year.
